# Model Overview (for Diagnosis)

Diagnosis targets the trained NextItNet through a host `ModelView`. Relevant hooks are `item_emb`, `log2feats(sequence)` and `predict_score(features, items)`. Histories are truncated and left-padded; the sequence representation is selected at the maximum nonpadding index. Model implementation is not supplied here; structural analysis recognizes specific gated, causal convolution code and otherwise reports reachability as unknown.

# Diagnosis Inputs & Hooks

`DiagnosisProbe(view, device)` accesses the actual network through `view.model`, training histories through `view.user_train`, and compatibility scoring hooks through the view. The loader supplies `(None, sequence, positive, negative)` tensors shaped B × L. Diagnosis runs without gradients, switches to evaluation mode, and restores module modes and random-generator states afterward.

# Probes & Metrics

- **Embedding alignment:** samples up to 2,048 item embeddings and maps mean off-diagonal cosine to [0,1]. Around 0.5 indicates near-zero mean cosine; higher alignment alone does not establish collapse.
- **Training margins:** measures aligned positive-minus-negative logits over ten loader batches. Larger margins and lower negative-win/small-margin rates indicate stronger sampled training separation.
- **Training-prefix ranking:** samples up to 12 users and two prefixes each, scoring eligible catalog items in chunks. Reports exact target ranks, user-averaged HR@10, scores and margins against up to 99 fixed negatives.
- **Intervention effects:** reports changed-minus-clean rank, HR@10, target score, margin and top-ten overlap. Positive rank change means deterioration; sensitivity itself is not inherently good or bad.

# Perturbation & Tests

In-place replacements compare recent versus older positions at doses one and two, matching frequency bins and possible reachability. Random and training-transition-constrained replacements must succeed jointly. Fixed catalogs and shared restricted catalogs separate effects involving inserted candidates; inserted-item gains are recorded separately. Full and terminal-preserving permutations test order sensitivity.

Controls check ranking ties, identical-input reproducibility, causal suffix isolation, all-padding features and applicable unreachable-position invariance. Numerical discrepancies should be near zero.

# MODEL_DIAGNOSIS Schema & Limitations

Output contains `metrics` and `metric_definitions`, including protocol, coverage, failures, architecture, aggregate effects, strata, raw observations and diagnostic cost. Aggregation weights users equally; exploratory user-bootstrap intervals and corruption Monte Carlo errors describe different uncertainty sources.

These are training-fit and sensitivity probes, not held-out generalization or causal preference evidence. Sparse matching limits support. Unavailable metadata, exact gated path counts and four-category macro results remain explicitly unavailable. Pinned host validation HR@10 governs selection.
